The Court Made The Following:
 Order

Petitioner who is arraigned as accused No.1 has filed this petition under Section 438 of Code of Criminal Procedure (for short, 'Cr.P.C.') seeking anticipatory bail in Crime No.47/2023 of Haveri Women Police Station for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 323, 354, 114 r/w Section 34 IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961.
2. In support of his petition, petitioner has contended that he is innocent of the offences alleged.
The allegations made against him does not attract the ingredients of the offences alleged in the complaint.
The alleged offence took place on 04.04.2023.
However the complaint is lodged on 06.07.2023.
There is inordinate delay of three months in filing the complaint.
No prima facie case is made out against the petitioner.
Already anticipatory bail is granted to accused No.2 to 4.
Petitioner NC: 2023:KHC-D:9043 is ready and willing to abide by any conditions that may be imposed and prays to allow the petition.

3. Learned High Court Government Pleader submitted oral objections stating that the marriage of complainant and petitioner was performed on 07.05.2019 and at the time of marriage, all the accused persons including the petitioner demanded and received dowry in a sum of Rs.8,00,000/-
and gold ornaments weighing 8 tolas and sarees and household articles worth Rs.1,00,000/-.
After the marriage, complainant was living with all the accused persons.
However she was harassed and ill-treated for additional dowry.
After her parents and family members came and advised the accused persons, petitioner set up a separate residence at Chandapur, Bengaluru and was staying with complainant.
After one month, he quarreled with her and they came back to his parents' house and harassment continued.
3.1 On 04.04.2023, all the accused persons quarreled with her and assaulted her and driven her out of NC: 2023:KHC-D:9043 the house.
Later complainant came to know that accused No.1 has married one Akkamma and the marriage was performed by the remaining accused persons.
After coming to know about it, she has chosen to file complaint on 06.07.2023.
The investigation is going on and the custodial presence of the petitioner is required for the purpose of investigation and charge sheet is yet to be filed and prays to reject the petition.

4. Heard arguments and perused the records.

sentences.text: As per the complaint averments, marriage of complainant and petitioner/accused No.1 took place on 07.05.2019.
There is allegation of demand and receipt of dowry in the form of cash, gold ornaments and household articles.
According to the complainant, after marriage, all the accused persons including the petitioner started harassing and ill-treating her for additional dowry.

Though on the advise of her parents and family members, for a short period of one month petitioner set up a separate residence at Bengaluru, once again he quarreled with her NC: 2023:KHC-D:9043 and brought her back to the matrimonial home and ultimately on 04.04.2023, the accused persons have driven complainant out of the matrimonial home.
With regard to the said incident, complaint is not filed.
Only after the complainant came to know that petitioner has contacted a second marriage, she has chosen to file the complaint.
6. Accused No.2 to 4 have been granted anticipatory bail by the Sessions Court.
Though there is allegation of demand and receipt of dowry, it appears no recovery is made so far as offence u/sec.498A IPC is concerned.
Looking to the nature of allegations made, the custodial presence of the petitioner is not required for the purpose of investigation.

In the light of the fact that there is a delay in filing the complaint, taking into consideration the nature of the allegations, this Court is of the considered opinion that petitioner is entitled for anticipatory bail.
Ofcourse, interest of the prosecution is NC: 2023:KHC-D:9043 required to be safeguarded by imposing stringent conditions.

Accordingly, the following:
ORDER Petition is allowed.

In the event of his arrest in Crime No.47/2023 of Haveri Women Police Station,
registered for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 323, 354, 114 r/w Section 34 of IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961, petitioner/accused No.1 shall be released on bail subject to following:
CONDITIONS a) The petitioner/accused No.1 shall execute a personal bond in a sum of Rs.1,00,000/-
with two sureties for the like-sum.
b) Petitioner/accused No.1 shall appear before the investigating officer within a period of 15 days and execute the bail bond and offer surety.
c) Petitioner/accused No.1 shall make himself available for the purpose of investigation as NC:
2023:KHC-D:9043 and when required and he shall co-operate with the investigation.
d) Petitioner/accused No.1 shall furnish his residential address proof and shall inform the investigating officer/Court if there is any change in the address.
